# Lifecycle documentation

Select a task-oriented path through Lifecycle as an application developer, evaluator, platform operator, API user, or Agent administrator.

## Create, use, and operate Lifecycle Environments

Select the path that matches your task. An administrator can disable features
or add role gates. Thus, each guide identifies its applicable prerequisites.

## I develop applications

- [Create my first Environment](/docs/getting-started/create-environment) — Onboard a repository. Open a pull request. Make sure that the Services are
  deployed.
- [Use the Lifecycle UI](/docs/features/lifecycle-ui) — Find Environments. Examine build and deployment logs. Start available
  actions.
- [Configure lifecycle.yaml](/docs/schema/overview) — Select Services, branches, dependencies, builds, deployments, and webhooks.

## I evaluate or operate the platform

- [Understand the system](/docs/operations/architecture) — See the components, request flow, storage, identity, and trust boundaries.
- [Select an installation path](/docs/setup/install-lifecycle) — Compare the starter OpenTofu and existing-cluster Helm evaluation paths.
  Then, make sure that your selected path is safe.
- [Operate Lifecycle](/docs/operations/day-two) — Plan upgrades, backups, recovery, monitoring, and configuration changes.

## I automate Lifecycle

- [Use the CLI](/docs/features/cli) — Authenticate. Examine Environments. Follow status. Read logs. Start actions.
- [Use API keys](/docs/api-authentication/api-keys) — Create a scoped credential. Use authenticated v2 endpoints. Revoke the
  credential.
- [Use the HTTP API](/docs/api/overview) — Find the generated OpenAPI reference and understand authentication
  boundaries.

## I use or administer Agents

Deployment packaging, configuration, and role policy control Agent and MCP
availability. Check each page's availability boundary before you use its
workflow.

- [Check Agent Session availability](/docs/features/agent-sessions) — When your deployment makes the feature available, see the current Labs
  boundary. Then, launch a governed workspace.
- [Learn Agent administration](/docs/features/agent-administration) — See which models, instructions, permissions, tools, runtimes, and inspection
  controls are available in a deployment.
- [Connect to Lifecycle MCP](/docs/features/mcp-server) — Lifecycle MCP uses one URL and OAuth sign-in for the tools that your account
  permits.

If you are not sure where to start, read [What is
Lifecycle?](/docs/what-is-lifecycle) and the [terminology
reference](/docs/getting-started/terminology).
